items.title: Week ahead – Flash PMIs and PCE inflation in focus ahead of Thanksgiving
items.excerpt: With all this hawkishness already reflected in the latest dollar rally, investors are likely to turn their attention to next week’s flash S&P Global PMI data for November, as well as the second estimate of the US GDP for Q3 and the PCE inflation numbers for October. The PMIs will start the show on Monday, and they attract special attention as they will provide a first glimpse of how US business activity fared during the month of November. The employment and prices subindices will also be closely watched given the Fed’s dual mandate of full employment and price stability. On Wednesday, the second estimate of Q3 GDP will offer updated information on whether the world’s largest economy can withstand more rate increases, while the PCE inflation indices, the Fed’s favorite inflation metrics, will confirm whether expectations of additional rate hikes beyond December is justified.

items.title: Higher fuel prices seep into core inflation - Dallasfed.org
items.excerpt: Alexander Chudik, Lutz Kilian and Xiaoqing Zhou November 19, 2026 Fuel prices have been on a wild ride since late February 2026, when military strikes on Iran set off sharp moves in oil and fuel markets. Retail gasoline prices aside, the U.S. retail diesel price reached an all-time high, the jet fuel price is near its previous peak, and the heating oil price has set a new record. The U.S. price of natural gas, meanwhile, has barely budged. The fuel price surge has been very uneven. Diesel prices in particular moved sharply higher. Diesel is the fuel of the freight economy. Trucks, trains, ships and farm equipment run on it, which means its price may potentially touch the cost of moving nearly everything consumers buy. The price gap between diesel and gasoline has widened significantly in recent months. On Sept. 22, 2026, the national average retail price of diesel reached $6.53 per gallon, about 70 percent above its level at the end of February (compared with a 50 percent rise for retail gasoline). The diesel rise surpassed the fuel’s previous record set in 2022 (Chart 1). Prices have eased only modestly, to about $6.31 as of the end of October. Consumers experience these prices directly at the pump and indirectly on their utility bills. But fuel prices may also work their way into the prices of other goods and services, from airline tickets to paper towels. Economists call these "second-round effects," and they matter for the Federal Reserve because they show up in core inflation, an inflation measure that excludes food and energy. Policymakers watch core inflation closely to gauge underlying price pressures. Our estimates suggest that higher fuel prices added between 20 and 60 basis points to 12-month core inflation, as measured by the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index, as of September 2026. If fuel prices simply held at their current levels, that contribution would gradually decline by about 30 basis points by the end of 2027.

items.title: ’Black Friday’ brings consumer spending into focus for AI-rocked market By Reuters
items.excerpt: NEW YORK, Nov 20 (Reuters) - Investors will turn attention next week to the strength of consumer spending, as they hope evidence of a broadly solid economic backdrop can provide stability for a US stock market that has been shaken by unease about the AI trade. Next week, "Black Friday" heralds the onrush of the holiday shopping season as retailers offer a wave of discounts. Investors will watch for signs of how consumers are coping with inflation, including rising energy and borrowing costs. Consumer spending accounts for roughly two-thirds of the US economy. ... Oxford Economics estimates that holiday retail sales will rise 4.2%, or an increase of 2.2% in volume after adjusting for inflation. That covers retail spending in November and December, excluding autos, gasoline, and bars and restaurants. The National Retail Federation projects 182.7 million consumers plan to shop this year during the five-day Thanksgiving period that runs to "Cyber Monday", citing results from a recent survey. Black Friday is expected to be the most popular day to shop during that period. That overall number would be down slightly from 186.9 million last year, but continues the trend of elevated shopping during the holiday weekend in recent years, the NRF said. Government data this week showed US retail sales for October increased moderately, while the core measure of such sales rose faster than expected. Retailers including Walmart and Target had upbeat comments or outlooks for the holiday season in their quarterly reports this week. "The consumer is pretty healthy, and we’d like to see that continue ... COULD GASOLINE PRICES SAP SHOPPING? Despite solid retail sales data, Gene Goldman, chief investment officer at Cetera Financial Group, said he was worried "that the consumer is being impacted by higher gas prices, higher energy prices, higher food prices." The average national price for a gallon of gasoline stood on Thursday at $3.72, according to motorists’ group AAA. That is down from nearly $4.30 a month ago, but well above the $3.09 level a year ago.

items.title: Oil prices set for third straight weekly decline on Middle East export flows
items.excerpt: Oil prices rose on Friday but were set for a weekly decline as concerns over supply disruptions grew following Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh and reports of tanker disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz. ... Oil prices ⁠fell on Friday and were set for a weekly decline on strong exports from the Middle East despite Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia's capital ​Riyadh and reports of tanker disruptions in ​the Strait of Hormuz. Brent ​crude futures were down $1.65, or 1.79%, to $90.33 a barrel at 1032 GMT. US West Texas Intermediate futures for December were down $1.62, or 1.95%, to $81.59 a barrel, while the more active January contract was down $1.22, or 1.48%, to $81.22. Brent is on track ⁠for ‌a 6% decline for the week and the December WTI contract ⁠for an 8% weekly drop as expectations of a supply surplus grew because crude shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have returned to roughly pre-war levels. This would be the benchmarks' third straight week of decline.

The station’s playlist includes Asake’s Joha, Burna Boy’s Giza with Seyi Vibez, Phyno’s Do I (Remix) and William Onyeabor’s Fantastic Man. One thing worth clearing up: reports so far point to music and radio roles only. There is no confirmation that any Nigerian artist plays a character in the game. ... Seyi Vibez sets an Audiomack record ### What happened SWAGUU, the 14-track album Seyi Vibez released in September with Quavo on the title track, has crossed 200 million streams on Audiomack. It is the eighth of his ten projects to pass that mark, the highest number for any African act on the platform. Asake and Burna Boy are next with four each. SWAGUU has also been sitting at number one on the Audiomack and Boomplay album charts in Nigeria. ... ## 3. New Music Friday: Joeboy’s Lavida Boy and more ### What happened Joeboy released his Lavida Boy EP this morning. It has five songs: Easy Does It, Santorini with Ruger, Pretty Girls, which came out earlier this month, Jemima and Applause. Also out today is Artifeelicial, a five-song EP from Nigerian singer Soundz and London-based Ghanaian executive KJ Spio on Ziiki Media, which Apple Music has added to its New Music Daily playlist. From East Africa, Kenya’s Bien released a 17-track album, Alusa Continua, with Oxlade among the guests. ... ## 4. Nollywood gets ready for Christmas ### What happened MTN Nigeria and actress and filmmaker Omoni Oboli unveiled seven new Christmas films at a movie mixer in Lagos attended by actors, filmmakers and content creators. The partnership is meant to make local films easier for audiences to find over the holidays. Separately, Femi Adebayo released the official poster for Jagun Jagun 2: War of Warriors, the sequel to his 2023 Yoruba epic, which arrives worldwide on Netflix on 4 December. And Dear Ajayi, Nigeria’s submission for the 2027 Oscars, is now on cinema screens after its Lagos premiere.
